$f$ is a logarithmic function, but its argument isn't simply $x$. Therefore, it's a composite function.

In other words, suppose $u(x)=x^2-1$, then $f(x)=\log\Bigl(u(x)\Bigr)$.

$f'(x)$ can be found using the following identity:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\log\Bigl(u(x)\Bigr)\right]=\dfrac{u'(x)}{\ln(10)u(x)}$

[[☃ explanation 1]]
